items.title: Recognition
items.description: [Revised entry by Mattias Iser on July 27, 2026. Changes to: Main text, Bibliography] Recognition has both a normative and a psychological dimension. Arguably, if you recognize another person with regard to a certain feature, as an autonomous agent, for example, you do not only admit that she has this feature but you embrace a positive evaluative attitude towards her for having this feature. Such recognition also implies frequently that you bear obligations to express this attitude in action, that is, treat her in a certain way. items.title: Liar Paradox
items.description: [Revised entry by Jc Beall, Michael Glanzberg, Ellie Ripley, and Lorenzo Rossi on July 26, 2026. Changes to: Main text, Bibliography, notes.html] The first sentence in this essay is a lie. There is something odd about saying so, as has been known since ancient times. To see why, remember that all lies are untrue. Is the first sentence true? If it is, then it is a lie, and so it is not true. Conversely, suppose that it is not true. We (viz., the authors) have said it, and normally things are said with the intention of being believed. Saying something that way when it is untrue is a lie. But then, given what the sentence says, it is true after all!...

items.title: Susan Stebbing
items.description: [Revised entry by Michael Beaney and Siobhan Chapman on July 24, 2026. items.title: Boundary
items.description: [Revised entry by Achille Varzi on July 17, 2026. Changes to: Main text, Bibliography] Whenever we think of an entity as distinct from its surroundings, we naturally think of a boundary. There is a boundary (a line) separating Maryland and Pennsylvania. There is a boundary (a circle) isolating the interior of a disc from its exterior. There is a boundary (a surface) enclosing the bulk of this apple. items.title: The Definition of Death
items.description: [Revised entry by Adam Omelianchuk and David DeGrazia on July 10, 2026. Changes to: Main text, Bibliography, notes.html] The definition of death involves matters of philosophy and public policy. The philosophical investigation of death has focused primarily on two questions: What is human death? and How can we determine that it has occurred? items.title: Wisdom in Contemporary Analytic Philosophy
items.description: [New Entry by Shane Ryan and Sharon Ryan on July 2, 2026.] What is wisdom? items.title: Cosmological Argument
items.description: [Revised entry by Bruce Reichenbach on July 1, 2026. It uses a general pattern of argumentation (logos) that makes an inference from particular, alleged facts about the universe (cosmos) to the existence of a unique being, generally identified with or referred to as God or Allah. items.title: Defaults in Semantics and Pragmatics
items.description: [Revised entry by Katarzyna M. Jaszczolt on June 30, 2026. Changes to: Main text, Bibliography] 'Default' can mean many different things in theories of meaning. It is so not only because of the multiplicity of approaches and dimensions from which meaning can be studied, but also due to the fact the theoretical landscape, as well as the societal implementations that are in the focus of public interest, are changing swiftly.
